description:
FILED s473t2 (Opus triage of the 152 causeless blessed sweep rows), on main 0d783d24.
PRE-EXISTING; probes scratch/s473t2/probes/p1-tie.pl, p2-inmem.pl, p3-cow.pl.

ROWS BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv): perl-tests/scalar.t 25, 30, 63, 73,
76, 78, 119 = 7 rows.

THREE PROBED SHAPES (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl on 0d783d24):

(a) NO GET/SET MAGIC -- and the proxy object LEAKS (p1-tie.pl):
      { package TS; sub TIESCALAR { bless {v=>'x'} } sub FETCH { $fetch++; $_[0]{v} }
        sub STORE { $store++; $_[0]{v} = $_[1] } }
      tie my $p, 'TS';
      open my $fh, '<', \$p; my $l = <$fh>; close $fh;
      print "read=[$l] fetch=$fetch store=$store";
    perl: read=[x] fetch=10 store=1
    PCL : read=[#<p-tie-proxy {1201A90083}>] fetch=0 store=0
    The SBCL print representation of the tie proxy reaching the program's own
    output is the runbook's "leaks an SBCL artifact" class.
    Rows 25 ("reading from magic scalars"), 30 ("FETCH only called once"),
    63/73 ("tied actions - write"/"- read": PCL builds ':O:P:SK:P' where perl
    builds ':F:S():O:F:S(ABC):P:SK:F:S(DEF):P').

(b) THE WRITE-BACK STRINGIFIES WITHOUT THE `""` OVERLOAD (p3-cow.pl):
      package lrcg { use overload fallback => 1, '""' => sub { 'chin' } }
      my $bovid = __PACKAGE__;
      open my $h, ">", \$bovid; print $h "the COW with the crumpled horn";
      seek $h, 3, 0; $bovid = bless [], lrcg::; print $h 'mney'; print $bovid;
    perl: chimney        PCL: ARRmneyx1)   (the default ARRAY(0x1) form, overwritten at offset 3)
    In perl-tests/scalar.t the same statements leave $bovid as the blessed ref,
    so the row reads 'chin' (rows 76 "writing to refs" and, as its consequence,
    78 "writing to numeric scalar" -- 78 agrees with perl in isolation).

(c) `>>` STRINGIFIES A REF TARGET AT OPEN (p2-inmem.pl):
      my $x = \42; open my $r, ">>", \$x; print "ref=[", ref($x), "]";
    perl: ref=[SCALAR]   PCL: ref=[]
    Row 119 ("still a ref after opening for appending").  The `<` and `+<` forms
    are correct (ref.t/scalar.t rows 117/118 pass), so it is the append opener.

ONE MECHANISM: the handle materialises the target as a plain CL string at open
and writes a plain CL string back, so every per-SV behaviour (magic, overload,
the referent identity of a ref) is lost.  The fix belongs where p-open builds an
in-memory handle: keep the target BOX and go through the ordinary get/set-magic
and stringification helpers on every read/write.

Two of the blessed scalar.t rows now PASS on the s507p tree: 25 "reading from magic scalars" and 30 "FETCH only called once" -- #2111 makes a '<' in-memory handle read its scalar LIVE through the box, so the tied scalar's FETCH fires (once).  Baselines edited by hand (eb32f524); main fee16466 measures scalar.t 86/30, the tree 88/28.  The overload write-back and the `>>` ref-target rows remain.
